market_commentary:
The Strait of Hormuz crisis and ceasefire dominated the two-week period ending April 13, whipsawing commodity prices while equities advanced — WTI crude collapsed 34% from a peak near US$128/bbl (Apr 2) to US$83.85 after the strait reopened Apr 1740, while Brent dropped 9.0% in a single session to US$90.3815. The S&P/TSX Composite rose 1.7% to ~34,052 (+41% Y/Y)24, and the S&P 500 posted a record close at 7,022.9525. The Canadian dollar strengthened 1.5% to 0.7305 CAD/USD27 as the DXY fell toward 98, and the Bank of Canada held at 2.25% for a seventh consecutive meeting1. The project database tracks 7,344 projects valued at $1.37 trillion.

The oil price reversal split the pipeline’s commodity exposure in two directions — 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) carry direct WTI exposure, with the WCS differential widening to $16.25/bbl below WTI on Apr 1341. On the metals side, gold reached US$4,728/oz (+2.82%)17 and copper climbed to US$6.07/lb (+3.32%)19, referenced by 364 mining projects totalling $159.5B. The 10-year Government of Canada bond yield stood at 3.47%29 with the 2-year at 2.80%28, a 67-basis-point spread, against 211 residential ($44.4B) and 1,671 infrastructure projects ($179.0B) carrying financing cost exposure to rate movements.
